1.1.44 — A new look

  • A new command bar. ⌘L brings up a sheet of milky glass over the page, like Spotlight, with one-line results, a round go button and a soft wash of color along the bottom.
  • Controls in the sidebar. Back, reload and the address now sit at the top of the sidebar, and the page fills the rest of the window. Settings › Appearance moves them back onto the page if you prefer.
  • A quieter New Tab. One white search box in the middle of the page, with a mic for dictation.

1.1.43 — Calmer glass

  • Real glass, not so bright. The address and buttons above the page are shaded Liquid Glass that takes on the page behind it without glaring.
  • No white strip. Settings and the New Tab page get a bar that matches them in dark mode.
  • A softer arrival. Close the sidebar and the bar fades into focus, drifting in from the side, instead of dropping down from the top.

1.1.42 — Meet calls float

  • Your call, in the corner. Switch away from a Google Meet call (or press ⌃⌘P) and the whole call floats in a small window that stays on top, live, on every desktop.
  • Controls right there. Hover it to mute, turn your camera off, raise your hand or leave. Drag the top edge to move it, the edges to resize.
  • Back in one click. The button in the corner, or the call's tab, puts it back where it was. Leaving the call does too.
